narrative.overview: Every answer roost gives is set as a numbered data sheet in the International Typographic Style: typed fields on a strict grid, ruled in ink, with the one line that matters marked as if by highlighter. The page refuses the chat thread and the rounded-card dashboard. The system is quiet by default and dense where it counts: white paper, black ink, one grey for everything secondary, and a single signal colour on exactly one line per answer.
keyCharacteristics: White sheet, black ink, square corners everywhere.
One self-hosted grotesk (Schibsted Grotesk) in two weights.
Numbered field rows separated by hairlines and closed by ink rules.
Highlighter yellow behind the action line, and nowhere else.
Priority shown by the form of a square mark, not by colour.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: Highlighter yellow marks exactly one line per answer: the action quoted from the source file.

rules.name: The Ink Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Hairline grey separates rows inside a group; ink closes a group. Never ink between ordinary rows.

rules.name: The Dates-Only Tabular Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures apply to dates only; in Schibsted Grotesk tnum also widens . and , so scores stay proportional.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Only 400 and 700. Emphasis is weight or size, never italics, colour or tracking.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs separating, give it a rule or space, never a shadow or a card.

dos: Do keep yellow behind the action line only (The One Line Rule).
Do show priority by mark form plus the word, never by colour alone.
Do say where every value came from: the file name on the sheet, and a caption naming the list the action was quoted from.
Do render all document text with textContent; it is user content.
Do keep every corner square and every rule 1px (2px for a head, 4px for focus on the question field).
donts: Don't add rounded cards, shadows, gradients or coloured badges; the sheet is flat paper.
Don't make it a chat: no bubbles, avatars or streamed prose.
Don't draw birds, nests or twigs; the roost idea lives in the name and the copy.
Don't number lists whose order means nothing (the sample questions stay unnumbered); the sheet's field numbers stay.
Don't turn on tabular figures for scores or prose in Schibsted Grotesk (The Dates-Only Tabular Rule).
